newsitem.title: HONG KONG: PRESS DIGEST - H.K. Newspaper Editorials - Nov 7.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - H.K. Newspaper Editorials - Nov 7.

text.p: NOTE: These are highlights of comments in the Hong Kong press. The views expressed are those of the newspapers quoted, and do not represent an editorial viewpoint of Reuters.
- With 236 days to go before the British colony reverts to China, editorials in the Hong Kong media concentrated on the results of the U.S. presidential election.
The middle of the road MING PAO DAILY said that Bill Clinton was expected to develop a clearer China policy based on his experiences of dealing with the Chinese in the past four years.
It said that Clinton would focus on increasing the market share of U.S. goods in China, and stablising Sino-U.S. relations.

The SING TAO DAILY said The United States' China policy would not change much and conflicts could not be avoided because of the differences between the two countries in terms of national interests, views on human rights and the Taiwan issue.
The Beijing-funded TA KUNG PAO said that Hong Kong is not a country or a political entity and so, it needs a special way which suits its circumstances to produce its leaders.
It said the elections of some so-called western democratic countries were not really democratic.
For example, it said, the U.S. president was elected by only about 500 voters. It said what Hong Kong people needs is a democracy which suits Hong Kong and will be developed gradually.
The English-language SOUTH CHINA MORNING POST said that achieving a working relationship with China should be top of the list of Clinton's things to do.
It said that Washington and Beijing can set a longer-term strategy to prevent the relationship being blown off course by storms over trade, human rights, arms proliferation and Taiwan.
